title: ～んだって
shortExplanation: Conveys information heard from someone else; 'I heard', 'They said'.
longExplanation: The ～んだって grammar point is used to relay information the speaker has heard from someone else. It's a casual way of quoting what was said, effectively combining explanatory のだ (んだ) with the informal quoting particle って. It can be translated as 'I heard...' or 'They said...'.
formation: Verb-casual + んだって, い-Adjective + んだって, な-Adjective + なんだって, Noun + なんだって

examples.jp: 彼は東京に行くんだって。
examples.romaji: Kare wa Toukyou ni iku n datte.
examples.en: I heard he's going to Tokyo.

examples.jp: この映画、面白いんだって。
examples.en: They said this movie is interesting.

examples.jp: 彼女は有名な歌手なんだって。
examples.romaji: Kanojo wa yuumei na kashu na n datte.
examples.en: I heard she's a famous singer.

examples.jp: あのレストラン、夜景がきれいなんだって。
examples.romaji: Ano resutoran, yakei ga kirei na n datte.
examples.en: They said the night view at that restaurant is beautiful.

usageNote: Casual, spoken hearsay - "I heard (that)...", conversational tone.
